name: Membership Query Complexity
definition: The **Membership Query Complexity** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the minimum worst-case number of membership queries needed to identify an unknown target in $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: Minimum worst-case number of membership queries needed to identify the target.
origin_references: Membership queries in the exact query-learning model are introduced in \cite{angluin1988queries}.

monotonic.proof: A membership-query decision tree identifying every target in a class also identifies every target in a subfamily, without changing its queries or worst-case depth.

c_monotonic.proof: A membership-query learner for the original class learns a conditioned fibre by answering every query on a fixed coordinate for free and simulating all other queries.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{0001,0011,0100,1000\}$ has membership-query complexity 2: query the last coordinate, then use the third coordinate on the 1-branch and the second coordinate on the 0-branch. Projecting away the last coordinate gives $\{000,001,010,100\}$, for which every first query isolates at most one target and the remaining three require two further queries, so the complexity is 3.
